group.passage: Today people sing karaoke in bars, in private rooms and even at home. Few of them know that one of the men who made it popular could not read music. His name was Daisuke Inoue, and his story shows that a good idea does not always make its inventor rich. Inoue was born in Osaka in 1940 and took up the drums in high school. By 1970, he was playing in clubs in Kobe with six other musicians. Customers there often asked the band to play while they sang. Because Inoue could not read music, he learned to follow each singer by watching the singer's lips. One day, the head of a small steel company asked him for a favor. The man was going on an overnight trip to a hot spring and wanted to sing there, so Inoue recorded his music on a tape for him. Then an idea struck Inoue. If a company boss could sing to taped music, ordinary people in small bars could do it too. In 1971, Inoue and his friends had 11 machines built, each with an amplifier and specially made tapes, and began renting them to bars in Kobe. He recorded the songs in keys that ordinary singers could manage. The idea caught on fast, but Inoue never cashed in on it. He did not apply for a patent, so electronics companies soon made and sold their own machines, and he earned almost nothing from them. He was not the only inventor, either. In 1967, a Tokyo businessman named Shigeichi Negishi had already built a sing-along machine, and he never got a patent for it. By the 1980s, karaoke boxes with private rooms had spread across Japan. In 2004, Inoue received a prize for giving people a new way to learn to put up with one another. Strangely, he did not sing karaoke himself until his 59th birthday.

translation_zh.text:
今天，人們在酒吧、包廂，甚至家裡唱卡拉 OK。很少人知道，讓它流行起來的人之一竟然不會看樂譜。他的名字是井上大佑，他的故事說明好點子不一定會讓發明人變得有錢。
井上 1940 年出生於大阪，高中時開始打鼓。到了 1970 年，他和另外六位樂手在神戶的俱樂部演奏。那裡的客人常請樂團伴奏，讓他們唱歌。因為井上不會看譜，他學會看歌手的嘴唇來跟上每一位歌手。
有一天，一家小鋼鐵公司的老闆請他幫個忙。這個人要到溫泉去過夜旅行，想在那裡唱歌，所以井上把自己的演奏錄在錄音帶上給他。接著井上靈機一動：如果公司老闆可以跟著錄好的音樂唱歌，小酒吧裡的一般人也可以。1971 年，井上和朋友請人做了 11 台機器，每台都有擴音器和特別錄製的錄音帶，開始出租給神戶的酒吧。他把歌曲錄成一般人唱得上去的音調。
這個點子很快就流行起來，但井上從來沒有靠它賺到錢。他沒有申請專利，所以電子公司很快就自己做機器來賣，他幾乎什麼都沒賺到。而且他也不是唯一的發明人：1967 年，一位名叫根岸重一的東京商人就已經做出一台伴唱機，而他也從沒為它取得專利。
到了 1980 年代，有包廂的卡拉 OK 店已經遍布日本。2004 年，井上因為「給了人們一種學習彼此包容的新方法」而得到一個獎。奇妙的是，他自己直到 59 歲生日才第一次唱卡拉 OK。
